title: Auction day lures
takeaway: Refunds and claims happen only on the official site announced in advance, and never ask you to pay to "verify" first.

cards.title: Your refund is ready?
cards.body: The public auction ended an hour ago. You bid more than the final price, so you expect some ETH back. Then a DM arrives. It knows the auction, it sounds friendly, and it asks for a small payment first.

seg.label: Friendly greeting
seg.why: Friendly words are not the problem.

seg.label: Pay first request
seg.why: Real refunds never ask you to send ETH first.

seg.label: Unofficial claim site
seg.why: Not announced by the official accounts.

cards.title: How the auction refund works
cards.body: On Nov 30 the public auction runs for 24 hours. Every winner pays the same final price, set by the lowest winning bid. If you bid more, you claim back the difference. The team said full auction details come closer to the time. Claims happen only on the official site, announced in advance.
points: Claim links come only from official accounts.

cards.title: Pay to verify is always a lure
cards.body: No real refund or prize makes you send ETH, a fee or a deposit to anyone first. If a claim costs anything, it is only the normal network fee shown in your own wallet, for a claim you started on the official site. A DM saying you won is not a win.
points: Links in replies are not official.

cards.title: Dragon Guard has nothing to claim
cards.body: Scammers borrow any trusted name, even this course. Dragon Guard has no badge to claim, no NFT, no wallet step. A Guardian NFT or Dragon Guard reward link is a lure. pdtools will never ask for your wallet, your seed phrase or a signature.
points: No pdtools page asks for your wallet.

questions.stem: You bid 0.08 ETH. The final price is 0.05 ETH. What happens to the extra?
options: You claim back the difference on the official site
It is kept by the team as a fee
It comes back by itself, with no claim
Support sends it to you after a DM
questions.why: Every winner pays the same final price. If you bid more, you claim back the difference on the official site.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting is not the problem.

seg.label: Unasked support message
seg.why: Real support never DMs you first.

seg.label: Send gas first
seg.why: Refunds never need you to send ETH first.

seg.label: Stranger's address
seg.why: Sending to this address only pays the scammer.

questions.why: Support never DMs first, and no refund needs you to send ETH to an address. Check the official site from your bookmark.

questions.stem: A DM says you won the auction and must claim within 10 minutes. What do you do?
options: Ignore it and check the official site yourself
Claim fast, auction wins do need claiming
Reply to ask if it is real
Share the link in chat to check first
questions.why: Wins and claims show on the official site announced in advance. A DM with a deadline is a lure.

questions.stem: A claim page asks you to send 0.01 ETH to verify your wallet before the refund. What is this?
options: A scam, real claims never need payment first
A normal network fee for the claim
A safety step the team added
Fine if the page has a lock icon
questions.why: Sending ETH to verify is always a scam. A real claim only shows the normal network fee in your own wallet.

questions.stem: Someone shares a link to claim a free Dragon Guard Guardian NFT. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, Dragon Guard has nothing to claim
Claim it, you earned it by finishing lessons
Connect only your mint wallet to claim
Ask the sender to share the contract
questions.why: Dragon Guard has no badge to claim, no NFT, no wallet step. Any Guardian NFT link is a lure.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Thank you message
seg.why: Thanks alone is not the problem.

seg.label: Unannounced refund site
seg.why: Not announced in advance on official channels.

questions.why: The rushed deadline and a refund site never announced in advance are the signs. Check on a second official channel.

questions.stem: You want to be ready to claim your auction refund. Where will the real claim page come from?
options: The official Pocket Dragons accounts, announced in advance
The first reply under the auction post
A DM from an admin who wants to help
A search ad for Pocket Dragons refunds
questions.why: Trust only links from the official Pocket Dragons accounts, checked on two channels and announced in advance.

questions.stem: A reply under the official auction post offers a faster refund link. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, replies are not official channels
Use it if it has many likes
Use it if the name looks official
Try it with a small amount
questions.why: Anyone can reply under a post and copy a name. Replies are where fake links hide.

questions.why: The domain was never announced, and the page asks you to pay to verify. Close it and check the official accounts.

questions.stem: A stranger's refund site opens a wallet request that says Permit and names a spender. What do you do?
options: Reject it and close the site
Sign it, refunds need permits
Sign it, signatures cost no gas
Sign it, then revoke later
questions.why: A Permit signature can let the spender take your tokens without gas. A refund never needs one from a stranger's site.
